proposed_rules.description: OAuth consent classification must process only the normalized OAUTH_CONSENT_ABUSE indicator as Evidence-first HIGH/WARN without performing OAuth, token, provider, browser, mailbox, network, response, or deployment operations.
examples: classify_oauth_consent_abuse validates tenant and untrusted-observation boundaries via _validated_observation, marks data as UNTRUSTED_DATA, locks mode/action/response/deployment to DRY_RUN/DETECT_ONLY/False/DISABLED, excludes sender and URLs from audit Evidence, and returns deterministic finding.

result.reasoning_summary: FW-BME-04 correctly implements deterministic OAuth-consent-abuse classification meeting all stated requirements. The new classify_oauth_consent_abuse() function exhibits proper Evidence-first pattern: calls _validated_observation for tenant/authority revalidation, checks only for exact OAUTH_CONSENT_ABUSE indicator, audits before returning, excludes sender/URL from evidence record, and returns hardcoded HIGH confidence with WARN recommendation. Mode, action, response, and deployment are locked to DRY_RUN, DETECT_ONLY, False, and DISABLED respectively—all hardcoded for determinism. No OAuth exchange, provider call, token access, browser/mailbox/network operation, containment, remediation, deployment, or policy/response authority is added. Boundaries are maintained: observation validated against expected tenant via existing _validated_observation() with untrusted-data trust level explicitly recorded. The patch is narrow (4 files: status, queue, implementation, tests) with comprehensive boundary testing: test 1 verifies exact positive case with evidence minimization; test 2 validates benign/tenant-mismatch/authority-invalid/evidence-failure rejection paths. No syntax errors, no prohibited side effects, pattern reuse appropriate.
